text:
sarah: heads-up: seeing a sharp p99 spike for hosted /v1/generate around 14:06 UTC — baseline ~180ms, now ~700-900ms. p95 up a bit too but p99 is the noise. queue depth on pool-3 jumped, requests piling for ~200-400ms before entering kernel. paging eng-runtime.

nora: looking at console now — per-route p99 180 -> 820ms, p95 220 -> 360ms. traffic volume steady. interestingly KV cache global hit rate dropped ~15% for the last 30m on hotshard-7. kernel_selector metric shows flapping between primary and aux kernels (switch count up). grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/hosted-api (attached).

deploy-bot: deploy complete: hosted/batcher v2.14.3 -> v2.14.4 by jenkins at 13:58 UTC (commit d4c3f2b). CI: all green.

maya: I can reproduce with a low-QPS burst locally. behavior looks like batching heuristics + kv-prefetch interaction. when queue depth oscillates we build smaller batches but kernel_selector starts picking an aux kernel intermittently which increases per-token overhead. profiler shows kernel_selection() holding a lock longer during spikes.

omar: quick profiler dump from a reproducer:
```
# profiler sample (hot stacks)
kernel_selector.cpp:142 select_kernel() 47%
batcher.cpp:88 assemble_batch() 22%
kvcache.cpp:312 lookup_many() 15%
network_io.cpp:45 send_chunk() 8%
```

li: eviction rate increase matches a recent prefetch tuning change (rolled in v2.14.4). prefetch now probes more aggressively and seems to thrash hot shard's KV cache under certain priming patterns — that would lower hit rate and force more kernel work + IO. could be a noisy-tenant priming storm (tenant T-42 seen doing lots of short priming requests).

maya: mitigation options: 1) temporarily lower prefetch aggressiveness to prior threshold, 2) pin kernel selection to primary for hosted route until we stabilize, or 3) reduce max_batch_tokens to force more predictable batch shapes. low blast radius change: set max_batch_tokens=256 and enable prefer_aux_fallback=false for this route.

nora: applying quick patch to hosted routing config: set max_batch_tokens=256 for /v1/generate on pool-3, prefer_aux_fallback=false. rolling restart batchers on pool-3 now.

nora: patch applied and batchers restarted — took ~90s to roll. observability update: p99 dropped from ~820ms -> ~260ms within 3 minutes. KV cache hit rate climbing back up.

sarah: nice. sounds like a combo of prefetch thrash + kernel flapping. next actions: create IR ticket, revert prefetch tuning in next canary, add more kernel_selector tracing, and add a per-tenant priming throttle to prevent noisy neighbors.

omar: logging plan: add a lightweight kernel_selector debug log (sampled) that records chosen kernel id, batch size, and kvcache hit ratio per batch. will be safe-sampled to 1/1000. also will add a small profiler probe around select_kernel.

li: I'll open rollback PR for prefetch threshold and link it to the IR.

nora: ticket created: INF-3421 — "hosted p99 spike: prefetch thrash + kernel flapping". logs attached and config diff.

sarah: marking this as mitigated for now, will monitor for 2 hours then close. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maria: (react) :eyes:  — watching but not directly involved.

nora: final check at 16:30 UTC: metrics stable, p99 ~210ms, KV hit > baseline. leaving mitigations in place until canary completes next week.

sarah: closing thread when canary is green. good work team.
